title: SLIM: Stochastic Learning and Inference in Nonlinear GMM Models
abstract: arXiv:2510.20996v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We propose SLIM (Stochastic Learning and Inference in overidentified Models), a new scalable stochastic approximation algorithm for nonlinear GMMs with many nonseparable moments and parameters. SLIM is shown to be consistent and asymptotically normal without a consistent initial estimator or a globally convex GMM criterion. Random-scaling and plug-in based confidence set constructions remain valid when computational uncertainty can be non-negligible relative to sampling uncertainty. An optional second-order refinement achieves full-sample GMM efficiency. We develop $J$-tests for SLIM. The theoretical results are extended to models with clustered data of unequal cluster sizes. Monte Carlo experiments for a nonlinear demand system with 576 moments and 380 parameters demonstrate computational gains and scalability to one million observations. translated_title: SLIM：非线性GMM模型中的随机学习与推断
translated_abstract: 我们提出了SLIM（过度识别模型中的随机学习与推断），这是一种新的可扩展随机近似算法，适用于具有大量不可分离矩条件和参数的非线性广义矩估计（GMM）模型。研究表明，SLIM无需一致的初始估计量或全局凸的GMM准则，即可实现一致性与渐近正态性。当计算不确定性相对于抽样不确定性不可忽略时，基于随机缩放和插件法的置信集构造依然有效。可选的二阶精化能够达到全样本GMM效率。我们为SLIM开发了J检验。理论结果还被扩展至具有不等聚类规模的聚类数据模型。针对包含576个矩条件和380个参数的非线性需求系统的蒙特卡洛实验展示了计算效率的提升以及对一百万个观测值的可扩展性。一个涉及480万大学毕业生的LinkedIn应用案例展示了聚类估计及……
tldr: 提出了SLIM这一可扩展的随机近似算法，无需一致初始估计量或全局凸准则，即可对具有大量矩条件和参数的非线性GMM模型进行一致且渐近正态的估计与推断，并可扩展至百万级观测数据和聚类数据场景。
en_tdlr: SLIM is a scalable stochastic approximation algorithm for nonlinear GMM models with many nonseparable moments and parameters, achieving consistency and asymptotic normality without requiring consistent initial estimators or globally convex criteria, while scaling to millions of observations and clustered data.
